question.prompt:
Convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB = 3,\) \(BC = 4,\) \(CD = 13,\) \(AD = 12,\) and \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ,\) as shown. What is the area of the quadrilateral?

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_12B_Q09_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Draw diagonal \(AC\), which connects the two sides of the given right angle. Because the quadrilateral is convex, this diagonal splits it into two triangles with disjoint interiors, so their areas add.

Triangle \(ABC\) is right at \(B\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AC=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5.
\]
Triangle \(ACD\) therefore has side lengths \(5\), \(12\), and \(13\). Since
\[
5^2+12^2=25+144=169=13^2,
\]
the converse of the Pythagorean theorem shows that it is right at \(A\), where the sides of lengths \(5\) and \(12\) meet. Using the perpendicular legs as base and height, the quadrilateral's area is
\[
\frac12(3)(4)+\frac12(5)(12)
=6+30=\boxed{36}.
\]
The answer is \(\text{B}\).
solutions.title: Split into two right triangles
